# Psalm 81 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choir director: on the Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing with joy to God — he's our strength! Shout with excitement to the God of Jacob!

**2** Start the music! Beat the tambourine! Play the sweet-sounding lyre and harp!

**3** Sound the ram's horn at the new moon, and again at the full moon for our festival!

**4** This is the law for Israel, an ordinance from the God of Jacob.

**5** He established this for Joseph's descendants when he marched out against Egypt. Then I heard a voice I didn't recognize:

**6** "I lifted the heavy load off your shoulders; I freed your hands from carrying bricks.

**7** You cried out in your misery and I rescued you. I answered you from inside the thundercloud. I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah

**8** Listen to me, my people — I'm warning you! Israel, if only you would pay attention!

**9** You must not have any foreign god among you. Never bow down to some other god.

**10** I am the LORD your God — the one who brought you out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it with good things.

**11** "But my people wouldn't listen to me. Israel refused to obey.

**12** So I let them follow their own stubborn plans. They did whatever they wanted.

**13** If only my people would listen to me! If only Israel would follow my ways!

**14** I would quickly defeat their enemies and turn my power against their oppressors.

**15** Those who hate the LORD would bow in fear before him, and their doom would be sealed forever.

**16** But I would feed you the finest wheat and satisfy you with honey from the rock."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **81:10**: This verse captures God's heart perfectly: 'I am the LORD your God... Open your mouth wide and I will fill it.' God isn't stingy — he's generous beyond imagination. We just need to receive.

- **81:13-14**: There's something deeply moving about God saying 'if only.' The Almighty Creator, longing for his people to just listen. It's not anger — it's heartbreak.

— PNEUMA
